title: Basic sciences as applied to paediatric surgery
objectives: Draw the timeline of foregut budding, tracheoesophageal septation and lung phases with weeks.
Trace the three fetal shunts and the changes at first breath.
State neonatal fluid, glucose and thermoregulation principles that change drug dosing.
Explain why aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol and tetracyclines need special caution in neonates.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

Almost every Paper 1 opens here. Examiners love tables you can draw in ninety seconds: pharyngeal-arch derivatives, lung-development phases, fetal shunts. These are pure recall marks — bank them.

### Embryology you must be able to draw

The respiratory diverticulum buds from ventral foregut endoderm at week 4; faulty tracheoesophageal septation gives the EA/TEF spectrum. Lung development runs embryonic (4–7 weeks), pseudoglandular (5–17), canalicular (16–25), saccular (24 weeks to birth) and alveolar (late fetal life through childhood) — surfactant, vascular maturation and septation decide viability, never one single week. Diaphragmatic components close by week 8; failure leaves the Bochdalek defect behind the CDH story. Germ-cell tumours trace to migrating primordial germ cells, which is why midline and gonadal sites dominate.

### Fetal circulation in one paragraph

Oxygenated blood crosses the placenta → umbilical vein → ductus venosus (bypassing liver) → IVC → right atrium → foramen ovale → left heart → brain and coronaries first. Deoxygenated return goes SVC → right ventricle → ductus arteriosus → descending aorta → umbilical arteries. At birth, cord clamping raises systemic resistance, lung aeration drops pulmonary resistance, and the three shunts close functionally — persistent patency is the pathophysiology behind PPHN-style questions.

### Neonatal physiology and pharmacology

High total-body water and low fat/protein binding expand the volume of distribution for water-soluble drugs; immature glucuronidation (chloramphenicol grey-baby risk) and renal clearance (aminoglycoside accumulation) prolong half-lives. Dose by weight, correct for prematurity, and monitor levels. Neonates lose heat fast (large surface area, little subcutaneous fat) and burn glycogen quickly — warm chain and glucose monitoring are never optional in theatre or transport.

### How it is asked

Expect: draw-and-label embryology tables, fetal shunt tracing with postnatal changes, fluid/electrolyte calculations, and mechanism-plus-toxicity drug grids (the chemotherapy question is really a pharmacology question in disguise).
